pred_reasoning_trace:
A 57-year-old man with stage cS4a mantle cell lymphoma in complete remission after induction chemoimmunotherapy presented in August 2018 with painful swelling of the calves. There was no evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection. He reported a brief gastroenteritis episode at that time. Diuretics gave transient relief, but over weeks the swelling spread to the upper extremities and trunk muscles. Systemic steroids and a short discontinuation of ibrutinib had no effect.

By November 2018, calf swelling worsened; examination was notable only for one slightly enlarged right inguinal lymph node. Laboratory tests showed elevated LDH and CK, with negative autoimmune serology. Analgesics provided minimal benefit. In January 2019, CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema. The patient’s condition deteriorated, and he was hospitalized with generalized muscle pain, ECOG performance status 3, massive edema (especially of the lower extremities), and extreme muscle tenderness. Neurologic exam showed only weak symmetric fist closure and shoulder lift; no focal deficits.

Initial evaluations were consistent with myositis of unknown cause. Ibrutinib and rituximab were discontinued. Laboratory testing revealed elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH, with reduced plasma protein, albumin, and IgG; leukocyte count was elevated. MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema. Muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates with variation in fiber size, centrally located nuclei, necrosis, and regeneration. The patient developed acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Troponin I rose further; ECG revealed a new right bundle branch block and repolarization disturbances, and he developed atrial fibrillation. Cardiac MRI confirmed myocarditis. Over the next days, increasing somnolence and personality changes were noted. Brain MRI was unremarkable, but spinal MRI demonstrated a hyperintense lesion concerning for myelitis. CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl.
